questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose my destination based on which university offered interesting subjects in sociology. In addition, I had heard good things about exchange to Edinburgh from a fellow student and I wanted to go to a place that was not too far from Denmark, so that I could easily get visits from friends and family.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy - UoE sends a lot of e-mails. A little too many in my opinion.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got assistance via e-mail. However, the system at UoE is very user friendly, so it was easy to find information. In addition, me and my friends that was also on exchanged helped each other out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: UoE is very helpful and provides you with a lot of information. However, at times the e-mail flow was very overwhelming with a lot of e-mails about the same things being send over and over again. This led to a feeling of information overload.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I could apply via the hos university.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That the quality of the accomodations varies a lot. My accomodation (Haddington Place) was very nice, clean and with very helpful staff. However, som of my fellow students didn't have the same experience.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration proces is very user friendly, as they use a website where you fill in your information.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My coordinator at KU and e-mail assistance from UoE.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very successful. I ended up with only one of the classes i originally applied for. However, UoE have two weeks where you can make course change request, so ended up with some other interesting courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply as soon as possiple. I was in the last round of applying, and I think I would have had less stressful time and end up with the courses i wanted if I applied earlier on.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is good for an exchange student that have to adjust to a new system, language and uniwork. However, the courses are very topic specific which can make it hard to align the courses and essays with your field of interest. Compared to my studies at KU I feel like I learn more during a semester at home, as we have more group work, longer assignments and work with more complex theories.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was pretty much the same. We had lectures and self studies. However the semester is shorter and there is more individual work than group based work.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:

questions.answer:

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't know that I had to buy my own duvet, pillow and kitchen stuff to my accomodation.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was less expensive, but you still end up using a lot of money going out as you want to socialise with the other students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot - UoE has a lot of societies so you can pick and choose from a large amount of different activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Film society. Very cosy and a chill way to meet new people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the highlands of Scotland – beautiful nature. And explore nearby cities by train. I went to Stirling, Linlithgow, Glasgow and Newcastle. Very cosy cities for day trips.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. People small talk more and are more polite in Scotland, but that is just a plus when you are new in town.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participate in the societies.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found it easy to tap into the scottish culture as scots are very nice and polite. The challenging part for me was to live with other exchange student from very different cultures. Here were some differences in relation to how one is social and treats common areas.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The cosy pubs where everyone is welcome (even pets and kids) and the very polite and warm scottish people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Apply for grants so you can afford a nice accomodation and life in general, commit to uniwork as it gives your everyday life structure and have fun in the city with fellow exchange students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to do indvidual uniwork and write essays.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I have gained the courage to throw myself into the academic world abroad and have proven to myself that I do not give up even though the process is extensive. Furthermore, it has been rewarding to meet new people and get the opportunity to explore another university and city with people who have the same enthusiasm to learn and try new things. On a personal level, I have generally become an even more independent person.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was challenging to be away from my friends, family and boyfriend. However, you learn that they are all there when you return home and that Scotland is not that far from Denmark if you want someone to visit/come home for a visit yourself.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
